item.title: Spherical Coordinates
item.description: Coordinate Map We use the spherical coordinates (r,\theta,\phi) defined by \begin{dcases} x = r \sin \theta \cos \phi, \\ y = r \sin \theta \sin \phi, \\ z = r \cos \theta, \end{dcases} where r \ge 0, \qquad 0 \le \theta \le \pi, \qquad 0 \le \phi < 2\pi.

item.title: Newton-Raphson Method
item.description: Newton-Raphson Method Take a vector-valued function f: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n, and assume that we want to find a root of f, that is, we look for x^* \in \mathbb{R}^n such that f(x^*) = \mathbf{0}.
